0.x: **Target:** **Srivijaya**, ruled by the **Sailendra** dynasty over the **Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java** and nearby islands.
**Result:** Srivijaya forced to accept Chola power; not annexed.
**Cause:** Srivijaya controlled the **Strait of Malacca**, harassed Tamil traders and blocked the **China route** – a **trade-driven** punitive raid, not colonisation.
**Earlier ties:** friendly under Rajaraja I – the Srivijaya king built the **Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam**.
The Cholas defeated the Pandya and Chera rulers and dominated peninsular India, and sent an expedition against the **Sailendra** empire and conquered some areas.
**"Chola Lake":** **K.A. Nilakanta Sastri** – the Chola navy turned the **Bay of Bengal** into a Chola lake after **Rajendra I**'s expeditions.
**Maritime trade:** the South Indian dynasty of **maritime trade with South-East Asia** and China.
**Firsts:** **First Indian power to carry out overseas naval campaigns**; spread **Dravidian art** to South-East Asia.

**Born:** **Rajendra Chalukya** (counted as **Rajendra II** of Vengi), son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi.
**1075:** after **Vijayaditya VII** (last Eastern Chalukya) died, he **merged Vengi** with the Chola state – uniting Tamil and Andhra kingdoms.
**Last Chalukya-Chola ruler in Vengi:** **Parantaka Chola**; then the **Mandalika Yugam** (**1076 to c. 1210**).

**Viceroys:** Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola; commander **Gonka I**; installed **Anantavarman Chodaganga** in Kalinga), Vira Chola, Rajaraja Chola Ganga (crowned at **Jananathapura = Draksharama**; **Tekkali** inscription).
**Sri Lanka:** **Vijayabahu I** made the island independent; Kulottunga accepted it and married his daughter to the Sinhala prince **Virapperumal**.
**Decline after him:** weakening central bureaucracy, growth of **local chieftains**, rise of the Pandyas.
